pr.author: cjgillot

analysis.originalLogic: `RenameReturnPlace` (NRVO) looks for MIR that always copies the same local into the return place and eliminates the copy by renaming all uses of that local to `_0`. Its documented eligibility requires two conditions: "The return place must not be read prior to the `Return` terminator." and "A simple assignment of a whole local to the return place (e.g., `_0 = _1`) must be the only definition of the return place reaching the `Return` terminator." The pass then renames every use of the selected local to `_0`, removes the `_0 = local` assignment and storage annotations, and copies the local's debug declaration onto `_0`. In the reverted state, `DestinationPropagation` ran at `sess.mir_opt_level() >= 2` and after `DeadStoreElimination::Final`; the revert restores `DestinationPropagation` before `SimplifyConstCondition::Final`, restores `RenameReturnPlace` after final DSE, and raises the destination-propagation gate back to `sess.mir_opt_level() >= 3` because of the documented keccak perf regression.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: In the `wrong` custom-MIR regression, the original MIR performs `_2 = _1; _0 = _2; _2 = const 'b'; return;`. `RenameReturnPlace` renames the later write to the selected temp as well, producing `_0 = _1; _0 = const 'b'; return;`: the post-copy overwrite of `_2` becomes an overwrite of the return place, changing the returned value. The eligibility scan finds the `_0 = _2` assignment while scanning backward from `Return`, but does not reject a subsequent write to `_2` after that copy. The pass is therefore guarded by "// unsound: #111005" and is enabled only by `sess.mir_opt_level() > 0 && sess.opts.unstable_opts.unsound_mir_opts`. The revert restores this guard and also restores the opt-level-3 gate for `DestinationPropagation`; the old `DestinationPropagation` output for the same test (`nop; _0 = _1; _1 = const 'b';`) preserved the return value, so the miscompile test is attributed to the replacement NRVO pass, not to destination propagation.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions where a temporary local is assigned wholesale to `_0` and then written again before `Return`, especially custom MIR with exact statement order (`_2 = _1; _0 = _2; _2 = const 'b'; return;`). Also relevant: MIR affected by `DestinationPropagation` pass ordering relative to dead-store elimination and by the `mir_opt_level` gate, such as the `tests/mir-opt/dest-prop/union` case where a dead `_2 = const 1_u32;` is visible before DSE but becomes `nop;` when destination propagation runs after DSE.
analysis.summary: Reverting the destination-propagation-default change restores NRVO only behind `unsound_mir_opts` and restores `DestinationPropagation` to opt-level 3 and to a pre-DSE pipeline position. The reusable correctness lesson is that NRVO's whole-local rename to `_0` is unsound when the selected temp is overwritten after the copy to the return place; the later write is renamed into `_0` and clobbers the returned value.
analysis.trigger: NRVO candidate local is copied to the return place and then assigned again before `Return`; additionally, enabling `DestinationPropagation` at `mir_opt_level >= 2` instead of `>= 3` and placing it after final DSE changes which MIR it sees.
preconditions: The function has an NRVO-eligible local: the return place is not read before `Return`, and a whole-local assignment to `_0` reaches every `Return`.
The selected local is a `Temp`, not an `Arg`; `LocalKind::Arg` returns `None`.
A write to the selected temp occurs after the `_0 = temp` copy and before `Return`, which the eligibility scan does not exclude.
`DestinationPropagation` requires `sess.mir_opt_level() >= 3` after the revert, and runs before `&o1(simplify_branches::SimplifyConstCondition::Final)` in the restored pipeline.
pitfalls: Do not conflate address-taking/borrowing with the miscompile: the simple `nrvo` test takes `&mut _2` and is correctly rewritten to `&mut _0`; the unsound case is a post-copy overwrite of the temp.

Do not treat the old `DestinationPropagation` output as the clobbering transformation for the `wrong` test: it produced `_0 = _1; _1 = const 'b';`, while `RenameReturnPlace` produced `_0 = _1; _0 = const 'b';`.
A retained test name or comment does not establish that the replacement pass is incorrect; compare the actual value assignments before and after each pass.
The pass may overwrite `_0`'s debug declaration with a local of a different but layout-compatible type, e.g. `&mut T` instead of `&T`; this is documented as expected, not the miscompile.
This PR is a revert and no compiler was built or executed; MIR expectations in the patch are historical diffs, not reproduced runtime results.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/mir-opt` before/after MIR dumps with `//@ test-mir-pass: RenameReturnPlace` and `// EMIT_MIR nrvo_miscompile_111005.wrong.RenameReturnPlace.diff`, plus `//@ test-mir-pass: DestinationPropagation` for destination-propagation cases. Build custom MIR that differs only in statement order: copy temp to `_0`, then overwrite the temp before `Return`, and assert that the overwrite remains on the temp rather than becoming `_0 = ...`. Keep both panic-abort and panic-unwind variants; include the simple `nrvo` case with `&mut` to distinguish borrowing from post-copy overwrite. For `DestinationPropagation`, check the expected MIR diff under the opt-level-3 gate and the restored pre-DSE pipeline position. Do not claim execution or reproduction.
